uncited: - **Exact Boundary (Value 1.0):** If a normalized coordinate is exactly 1.0, `floor` yields $N$, which is out of bounds for an array of size $N$.
- **Periodic Wrapping:** Modulo of negative numbers in some languages (e.g., C++) returns negative results.
- **Out-of-Bounds Handling:** Indices may fall outside the grid dimensions $[0, X)$, $[0, Y)$, $[0, Z)$.
Converts continuous floating-point coordinates into discrete integer grid indices by rounding to the closest integer value [Child Note].
It serves as the fundamental coordinate quantization step in volume rendering, mapping sample points to voxel centers or corners [Child Note].

Unlike floor-based indexing which truncates towards zero or negative infinity, this method minimizes spatial quantization error by selecting the nearest grid node, which is critical for accurate gradient estimation and high-fidelity reconstruction [Child Note].
It differs from [Ceil](1574-ceil.md) which always rounds up, and [Floor](1575-floor.md) which always rounds down, by balancing bias in both directions [Child Note].
Choose it when minimizing spatial quantization error is prioritized over directional bias. [4233-nearest-integer-rounding.md]
The method originates from basic volume rendering techniques using 3D voxel grids.
